value.title: Unified error path and onError chain

acceptanceCriteria.text: With one recording `onError`, a `RuntimeException` thrown by a middleware, a checked `IOException` thrown by a handler and `next.error(e)` from a middleware each reach the handler once with the same `Throwable` instance and the request's `Request` and `Response`. [D-127; D-129; T36] Decision: a thrown `java.lang.Error` is not routed to `onError`; it aborts the response and is rethrown, as in wave 3. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-1]

An `HttpException(400)` thrown by a handler, an `HttpException(413)` and an `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` each reach `onError` with `status()` readable, and the malformed query `?x=%zz` raises an `HttpException` with status `400` that reaches `onError` after the middleware ran and before the handler. [D-129; D-130; wave-4 carried: malformed query]

With two `onError` handlers, the second runs only when the first returned with the response `NEW`, and receives the same error; when the first responded, the second records no call. [D-137] Decision: `onError` registrations form one chain in registration order that stops at the first handler that starts the response. Decision: the first `onError` handler runs whatever the response state was when the error arrived; a later one runs only while the response is still `NEW`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-2]

When every `onError` handler returned with the response `NEW`, or none is registered, the response is the standard error response of FR-APP-006 for the error. [D-132; D-137] Decision: the standard error response drops the status and headers the app set before the error. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-3]

An `onError` handler that throws makes the framework log the thrown exception at `ERROR` through the app logger and answer the standard `500` error response if the response is still `NEW`; no later `onError` handler runs. [D-129; D-133]

When a handler throws while the response is `STREAMING`, `onError` is still called once, no error body is written, and after the error path the response is `ABORTED` with the in-memory exchange closed abnormally; when the response is `COMPLETED`, it stays `COMPLETED` with the sent bytes unchanged. [D-131; T37]

A recording `onError` records no call for the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` and `OPTIONS` responses and for the pre-request and lifecycle-gate rejections. [residual: onError scope; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]

An error that ends in a standard `500` response is logged once at `ERROR` with its `Throwable` through the app logger; an `HttpException` with a `4xx` status is not logged at `ERROR`. [D-129; D-133] Decision: only `500`s are logged at `ERROR`, with the stack trace kept in the server log. Decision: a `500` is logged at `ERROR` whatever the response state, and no other status is logged at `ERROR`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-6]

The error path decides by the response state at the time the error arrives (`NEW` gives the error response, committed but not completed gives an abort, `COMPLETED` stays unchanged), the rule that the `res.json` serialisation case of D-136 relies on; that case itself is asserted in wave 5 once `res.json` exists. [D-136; D-131] Decision: the error path reads the response state once, after the `onError` chain, under the response lock; because a response committed on arrival can only stay committed or end, this gives the same outcome as the arrival-state rule. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-7]

value.requirement: The system shall route an exception thrown by a middleware or handler and an error passed to `next.error(e)` to one error path that calls the registered `onError` handlers in registration order while the previous one left the response `NEW`, writes the standard error response of FR-APP-006 when the response is still `NEW` after them, and aborts instead of writing an error body when the response is already committed but not completed, while `onError` never receives the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` or `OPTIONS` responses.
value.rationale: Covers D-127, D-129, D-131, the D-137 decision on `onError` chaining, D-136 (asserted in wave 5 once `res.json` exists) and the residual on `onError` scope. Replaces the wave 3 interim failure handling (FR-HTTP-006, superseded in wave 4). T36, T37.
